mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL increases do not correlate with subsequent FEDFUNDS hikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over three months signals a weakening labor market, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increases do not correlate with subsequent GDP declines.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a weakening demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS declines do not correlate with subsequent GDP declines.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increases do not correlate with subsequent GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals a potential overheating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and high CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent market declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs month-over-month signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increases do not correlate with subsequent GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% over three months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST declines do not correlate with subsequent GDP declines.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2%) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 2%, or low FEDFUNDS does not correlate with subsequent market performance.
